main_text.p: dixerunt lapidem istum veteribus il lis cognitum fuisse, quippe cuius Hippocrates mentionem fecerit in Epist. 9. ad Crateuam. Epistola ad Crateuam his verbis,τὸ ἡ χρῆμα τῆς ζοταν̃ων, παρά σοι πολλάκις ἐ- θωύμασα. ὡς ἢ τὴν ὅλωνγε φύσιν τε ἢ δια- ταξιν, ἡ τὸ ἱερώτατον γῆς ἵδρυμα. ἐξ ἧς τὰ ζῶα, ἡ φυτά, ἡ τροφαὶ, ἡ φάρμακα, ἡ τύχη, ἡ ὁ πλοῦτος αὐτὸς ἀναφύεται. ἃ ἢ γὰρ ἂν εἴ- χεν οἱ ἐπιδη̃, ἡ φιλαργυρίη. οὐ δ' ἂν Ἀβδη- ρίται μὲν νεῦ δέκα τοσαύτοις ἐδελέαζον, ἀντὶ ἵντρε μισθωτὸν ἐλέγχοντες. id est: At vero rem herbariam apud te, persæpe sum admi- ratus sicut etiam vniuersorum naturam & dispositionem: & constitutum sacrarium terræ, ex qua animalia, plantæ, & alimen- ta, & medicamenta, & fortuna, & ipsæ di- uitiæ exoriuntur. Nequæ enim, quo conce- deret, auaritia haberet. Neque Abderitæ me decem talētis nūc inescarēt, pro medico mer- cenariū declarantes. Hęc, in Epistola ad Crateuā. Sed vt nihil dicā de morosis criticis, qui fortasse negabunt Epistolam hanc esse Hippocratis: videntur verba hæc detorqueri in alienū sensum,

page.notes: The Greek is set in a small, worn type and several accents and breathings are doubtful; the Greek transcription is approximate. Marginal note "Epist. 9. ad Crateuam." is at the left. Printed text is sometimes irregular (e.g., "Crateuā", "Hęc"), left as printed.
